items.title: A whopping ₹28,000 crore deal! 🚀
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks and Happy Mondayyyy! ☀️

Indian markets rose on Friday despite weakness across global markets, with the Nifty 50 ending in the green.

What to watch: November’s monthly futures and options contracts expire on Monday, which could bring sharper market swings.

Globally, investors will watch Wednesday’s US inflation and economic growth updates for clues about interest rates and the economy’s health.

Friday and the weekend were quiet on the news front, but here’s what’s worth catching up on.

💡 Spotlight: A hefty oil & gas bill for India ⬆️

India’s net oil and gas import bill jumped 60% YoY to $16 billion in October, as the West Asia conflict and shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude prices sharply higher.

A quick rewind: the bill stood at $10 billion in October 2025. Brent crude averaged $124.7 a barrel this October, up from $64.75 a year earlier. India’s crude basket, the mix of oil it imports, averaged $119.91 a barrel, compared with $65.08 last year.

Why it matters: India imports nearly 89% of its crude oil needs, leaving it exposed to global price increases and supply disruptions.

Higher energy costs can raise expenses for businesses and households and weigh on economic growth.

A bigger safety cushion: India’s strategic oil reserves cover just 4.9 days of consumption. Expanding these emergency stocks could help cushion the country against supply disruptions and price spikes.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: A whopping ₹28,000 crore deal! 🚀

Tata Steel has agreed to sell its tubes business and its entire stake in Tata Steel Colours to APL Apollo Tubes in two deals worth up to ₹28,000 crore.

APL Apollo makes steel tubes and pipes used in construction, infrastructure and industrial projects.

Why the deal: APL Apollo says combining these businesses will increase production capacity, expand its distribution network and help it grow. For Tata Steel, the sales will bring in cash and simplify its portfolio of businesses that turn steel into finished products.

A chance to cut debt: Tata Steel’s net debt stood at ₹91,423 crore at the end of Q2 FY27. The sales could give it room to reduce that debt, though the company has not specified how it will use the proceeds.

What’s being sold:

  • Tubes business: valued at up to ₹11,700 crore. The sale includes manufacturing facilities in Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli and Sahibabad, along with certain steel-processing assets at Khopoli.

  • Tata Steel Colors: formerly Tata BlueScope Steel, the company will be sold for ₹16,300 crore in cash.

Tata Steel and Tata Steel Downstream Products (TSDPL) each own 50% of Tata Steel Colours. They will split the proceeds equally, receiving ₹8,150 crore each.

The business in numbers: Tata Steel Colours reported revenue of around ₹4,680 crore in FY26, accounting for 2.02% of Tata Steel’s total revenue. Its net worth stood at about ₹1,016 crore.

Once the deal is completed, Tata Steel Colours will no longer be a Tata Steel subsidiary.

Share

2. Deal frenzy 🤝

Voltas has agreed to acquire a 50% stake in Atomberg Airtech, a wholly owned subsidiary of Atomberg Innovation.

Why it matters: the companies will form an equally owned joint venture to develop, manufacture and sell room air-conditioner compressors and related parts in India.

Both partners have committed to investing up to ₹100 crore each. The money will be invested in stages, with the venture’s board deciding the timing and terms.

Meanwhile, Paytm is expanding in Singapore 💸

Paytm parent One97 Communications said its Singapore arm will invest up to ₹200 crore in subsidiaries of Singapore-based Funding Societies. This includes about ₹162 crore for a 19.1% stake in CardUp, its payments subsidiary.

The plan: One97 Communications will also partner with CardUp to provide payments and lending technology, expanding Paytm’s payments and financial services technology business in Singapore.

Share

3. How GTA 6 turned hype into billions? 👀

GTA 6 reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, nearly five times GTA 5’s launch-day sales.

But Rockstar’s biggest marketing advantage wasn’t a flashy advertising campaign. It was 13 years of anticipation, internet memes and millions of fans keeping the conversation alive, often without Rockstar saying a word.

Full Story Here

4. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🎬 Tips Films jumped 6% after announcing a voluntary delisting proposal, with promoters seeking to acquire the 25% public shareholding.

🏗️ Dilip Buildcon rose more than 4% after winning an order worth ₹419.5 crore.

💻 The Nifty IT index gained over 2% despite a global sell-off in AI stocks following Anthropic’s debut.

🔄 Shanti Educational Initiatives ended nearly 5% higher as BSE cleared its proposed restructuring agreement with its subsidiary.

🏥 Healthcare stocks, including Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals, gained up to 5% following a brokerage’s double upgrade.

What went down ⬇️

🪙 Titan, Muthoot Finance, and Kalyan Jewellers fell up to 4% as gold prices continued to slide.

❌ Ashoka Buildcon ended more than 2% lower after a Saudi Arabian firm cancelled an order worth ₹846 crore.

🤖 Hitachi Energy India, E2E Networks and other AI-linked stocks fell up to 5% as concerns about AI overshadowed Anthropic’s debut.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

🔺 Production boost: India’s core sector growth hit a 31-month high of 10.9% in October, led by iron ore, coal and electricity production.

📈 Market milestone: NSE became the world’s fifth-largest listed stock exchange operator at a $59.3 billion valuation, overtaking Nasdaq and HKEX as its shares rose nearly 25% since its September IPO.

😐 Price hike: Maruti Suzuki raised prices on select models by an average 0.31% from November 22 due to cost pressures despite cost-cutting.

⚖️ Payment dispute: Allied Blenders approached the Bombay High Court over unresolved payments and recoveries linked to Officer’s Choice whisky supplies to India’s military canteen network.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the Monday blues get to you.

We’ll be back on Wednesday, November 25th, as stock markets are closed tomorrow for Guru Nanak Jayanti.

items.title: Anthropic makes a stellar debut ⚡️
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks and Happy Fridayyyy! ☀️

Another day, another Nifty Bank-led rally. The index crossed the 63,000 mark for the first time, hitting a record high of 63,063. Meanwhile, the Sensex and Nifty gained more than 1% each.

Auto and FMCG stocks led the gains as falling commodity prices raised hopes of lower costs for companies.

On the other hand, IT stocks fell, with Infosys, Tech Mahindra, TCS and HCL Technologies among the biggest Nifty losers.

The rally added around ₹40 lakh crore to the value of BSE-listed companies in November, taking their combined market capitalisation to a record ₹512 lakh crore.

The Indian rupee also extended its winning streak on Thursday reaching a seven-month high against the US dollar as continued foreign investor purchases and easing crude oil prices provided support.

💡 Spotlight: India’s Scotch tax cut gets a hangover 🥃

Your Scotch may be getting costlier, and the first major fight under the India-UK trade agreement is responsible.

What happened: the trade deal implemented in July reduced India’s tariff on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%. It was supposed to make Scotch cheaper and help British liquor companies sell more in India.

However, Indian customs investigators argue that some bulk Scotch imports may be entering the country under the wrong product category.

These shipments are now being treated as “compound alcoholic preparations”, which attract a 150% tariff. An additional consumption tax takes the effective levy to 162.5% even higher than the duty charged before the trade agreement.

Meanwhile, liquor companies say Scotch remains Scotch whether it arrives in a retail bottle or a large container.

They believe both bottled and bulk Scotch should receive the reduced 75% tariff promised under the trade agreement.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: Anthropic’s stellar debut ✨

Anthropic, the company behind AI chatbot Claude, has made its Wall Street debut, with shares jumping 34% as trading began and pushing its valuation to around $2 trillion.

That would make it the world’s sixth-most valuable listed company.

The IPO in numbers:

  • Money raised: $81.3 billion

  • Shares sold: 980 million

  • IPO price: $83 per share

  • Valuation at the IPO price: $1.5 trillion

A big windfall for employees: according to SEC filings and investor estimates, Anthropic employees could own company shares worth more than $40 million each on average. Over 400 employees could have shares worth more than $100 million each.

At $83 per share, their combined shares would be worth around $232 billion. They would only receive cash when they sell, and some employees own far more shares than others.

At the opening bell: co-founders and siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the Nasdaq opening bell.

Dario highlighted AI’s potential to advance medicine and help cure diseases, while stressing the need to develop increasingly powerful systems safely. “An obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic’s DNA from the start,” he said.

Daniela Amodei urged people to help shape AI’s future. ‘This technology needs you, not your trust, not your use, but your voice,’ she told CNBC.

2. “Jointly Safeguarding World Peace” - no pressure then 🌍

Amid the Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran conflicts, the leaders of China, the US and Russia sat together to discuss “world peace”.

Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on Thursday for the first trilateral summit involving the leaders of all three countries.

The closed-door discussion at Kylin Villa lasted approximately one hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the three leaders were “making history”, while Xi called on them to “jointly safeguard world peace and stability”.

The meeting ended with a four-point Declaration Toward Peace covering nuclear weapons, energy supplies, the United Nations and international courts.

Everything they discussed:

  • The leaders agreed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. Their countries will begin discussions on reducing the risk of nuclear conflict and preventing more nations from obtaining nuclear weapons.

China has previously argued that the US and Russia must first reduce their much larger stockpiles before Beijing can be expected to make similar cuts.

  • Plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products.

The Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran conflicts have disrupted energy trade and shipping routes. Increasing fuel supplies could reduce shortages and help control global prices.

  • The leaders said they want to reform the UN so it can respond more effectively to global conflicts and security challenges.

  • As per the three leaders, international courts must respect the sovereignty of countries and should not “abuse” their authority.

  • Ukraine war, the Middle East and tensions on the Korean Peninsula were discussed behind closed doors.

3. LT Foods adds a US flavour 🌍

LT Foods, the company behind Daawat rice, has agreed to acquire 100% of MK Foods Holdings, the parent company of premium Indian-inspired food brand Maya Kaimal. The deal values the business at $5.8 million or about ₹54 crore.

The stock gained nearly 5% on the back of this news.

Why it matters: the acquisition will expand LT Foods’ range of ready-to-eat, ready-to-cook and ready-to-heat foods and strengthen its presence in the US packaged food market. The deal could also help the company reach more stores and customers.

What it’s buying: MK Foods Holdings owns Maya Kaimal Foods LLC, which sells Indian-inspired sauces, ready-to-eat curries and rice products.

MK Foods Holdings reported revenue of $17.9 million for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, up from $15.5 million a year earlier.

4. Why do US tech systems keep crashing? 😶

America has witnessed a series of major tech outages, disrupting everything from Microsoft services and banking transactions to airline operations.

While some suspect AI is behind the failures, the actual causes point to software bugs, ageing infrastructure and increasingly complex technology systems.

Full Story Here

5. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

📚 PhysicsWallah rose 6% after announcing FY30 revenue targets of ₹9,000-10,000 crore and EBITDA margins above 20%.

💪🏻 Maruti Suzuki jumped over 7% as aluminium, copper and other metals hit seven-month lows, easing concerns over input costs.

🌬️ Voltas, Blue Star and other appliance stocks rose 8-9% as copper, a key manufacturing material, hit seven-month lows.

🪖 Defence stocks rose, with the Nifty India Defence index gaining over 1%, after a request for 20% higher FY28 defence capital spending.

What went down ⬇️

💸 Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik fell 4-8% amid uncertainty over when the merchant discount rate (MDR), a fee merchants pay to accept certain digital payments, would take effect.

📉 PB Fintech fell up to 6% after co-founder and executive vice-chairman Alok Bansal decided to leave his executive role.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

🤖 Metaverse partnership: Infosys partnered with Japan’s NTT Docomo, taking a minority stake in a telecom venture to develop AI-powered virtual shopping experiences and digital twins.

📈 IPO filing: NLC India Renewables filed IPO papers for a ₹3,300 crore fresh issue, with parent company NLC India also planning to sell 10 crore shares in its green energy arm.

☀️ Solar partnership: Armee Infotech signed an MoU with MSEDCL for a ₹1,629 crore solar project with a capacity of 135 MW in Maharashtra.

🧋Funding round: Boba Bhai raised $18 million in Series B funding from Left Lane Capital, BIG Capital and Titan Capital to expand its stores across India.

And that’s a wrap. Pour yourself an extra one this weekend. 🥂

We’ll be back like clockwork on Monday!

items.title: India’s ₹1,976 crore shield at sea ⚓️
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks! ☀️

Before we get to deals, investments and earnings here is what everyone cannot stop talking about.

Grand Theft Auto VI, better known as GTA 6, has begun its phased global release. Gamers in New Zealand and Australia were among the first to play, and early reactions are already calling it “amazing.”

So yes, we really did get GTA 6 before some other long-awaited updates today. 😉

Now, let’s check the markets 📈,

Dalal Street took a breather on Wednesday, likely as investors booked profits following the recent rally.

Sensex and Nifty declined 0.6% each. The Nifty Bank lost 235 points but performed relatively better than the broader market.

Midcap stocks faced heavier selling, with the Nifty Midcap index falling more than 1%. Three stocks declined for every one that advanced, while 37 Nifty companies ended in the red.

Important to note that the latest Fed minutes showed that US Federal Reserve officials believe interest rates may need to rise again to control inflation. However, they kept rates unchanged in October while waiting for more economic data.

💡 Spotlight: SEBI may limit borrowed stock bets 🧾

Shares of BSE and Angel One reversed their gains and fell as much as 3% after SEBI said it was considering new limits on the Margin Trading Facility.

MTF allows investors to purchase shares without paying the entire amount upfront. So SEBI is considering limiting MTF-funded purchases in a stock to 5-10% of its free float.

Free float is basically shares available for regular investors to buy and sell. Shares held by promoters, governments or other long-term controlling investors are generally excluded.

Angel One lends money through MTF and earns interest and trading fees. BSE benefits when more shares are traded on its exchange. Investors worried that tighter limits could reduce borrowing and trading activity, affecting their revenue.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: ₹1,976 crore reboot for India’s naval shield 🚢

The Ministry of Defence signed a contract with Israel Aerospace Industries which covers Barak Point Defence Missile Systems already installed on Indian Navy ships.

What’s going on: this is not an order for a completely new missile system. India will upgrade the hardware and software of its existing Barak systems and replace components that are becoming too old to maintain.

Think of the Barak system as a warship’s personal security guard in the sky.

Why is this happening: threats to warships have changed considerably since the Barak system was first deployed.

Navies must now prepare for smaller drones, faster anti-ship missiles and attacks involving several weapons arriving together. Older electronics and software may struggle to handle these threats as effectively as newer systems.

The larger defence plan: the contract follows the Defence Acquisition Council’s approval of projects worth around ₹1.1 lakh crore in September. These included helicopters, radars, military vehicles, electronic jammers and upgrades for approximately 40 Su-30MKI fighter aircraft.

Zoom out: between 2021 and 2025, Israel supplied around 15% of India’s major arms imports, making it India’s third-largest supplier after Russia and France.

India was also Israel’s biggest foreign customer during this period, purchasing 29% of Israel’s major arms exports.

Share

2. Nvidia’s revenue doubles as AI demand surges 🚀

The chipmaker’s shares rose as much as 6% in extended trading on Tuesday after it reported strong third-quarter numbers and offered a confident outlook for the months ahead.

First, the record numbers: the AI giant’s revenue more than doubled year-on-year to $115.8 billion in Q3 FY27.

What fuelled earnings growth: Nvidia’s data-centre business remained the star of the quarter. It now contributes more than 90% of Nvidia’s overall revenue.

Data centres buy Nvidia’s powerful processors to train and run AI models. Demand from cloud companies, AI laboratories and other technology businesses therefore continues to drive most of the company’s growth.

Nvidia also began shipping its new Vera Rubin systems during the quarter. The company described it as the fastest product rollout in its history.

Beyond data centres: Nvidia’s edge-computing business generated $8.2 billion, up 42% YoY.

This segment includes chips and technology used in personal computers, autonomous vehicles, robotics and other devices that run AI locally instead of depending entirely on a distant data centre.

What comes next: Nvidia expects Q4 revenue of around $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

However, gross margin is expected to fall to between 71% and 72%. Management indicated that Q4 could mark the low point, with margins expected to improve afterwards.

For FY28, Nvidia raised its revenue growth outlook to approximately 75%, from its earlier projection of 70%. Gross margins are expected to recover to between 72% and 73%.

China remains the problem: the company has not included any revenue from selling data-centre computing products to China in its Q4 forecast.

New US restrictions seek to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced American AI chips, including through data centres located in other countries.

No Jensen comeback: Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones began the earnings call by addressing the leadership question directly.

He said the board had unanimously accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation and did not intend to reinstate him as CEO.

Share

3. India–South Korea deepen auto manufacturing partnership 🚘

NDR Auto Components jumped nearly 8% after it signed an agreement with South Korea’s DYA to manufacture complete passenger-car seats in India.

DYA designs and manufactures complete seats, including seat assemblies, cushions, headrests and armrests. Its major customers include Hyundai Motor and Kia in South Korea.

The deets: the two companies will establish a new joint venture in India where NDR Auto will own 51%, giving it majority control. DYA will hold the remaining, making the new company a subsidiary of NDR Auto.

The project will involve an investment of up to ₹63 crore.

The why: NDR currently manufactures automotive seating components such as seat frames and trims.

Through the new venture, NDR Auto wants to move from supplying individual components to designing and producing the complete seat system delivered to a car factory.

Zoom out: The NDR–DYA venture is positioning itself for that demand.

Kia recently announced a $2 billion investment, together with its suppliers, to build a second factory in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh. Meanwhile, Hyundai Motor Group is also investing $15.5 billion in India between 2026 and 2032.

While we are on investments,

Supreme Petrochem will invest ₹450 crore to build a second mass ABS production line at its Amdoshi plant in Maharashtra. It has partnered with Italy’s Versalis for the technology required to manufacture the plastic.

Supreme Petro manufactures plastics used by automobile, appliance, electronics and other consumer-product companies. Versalis is a chemical company which develops the technology and manufacturing processes used to produce specialised plastics such as ABS.

ABS, or Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene, is a strong but lightweight plastic that can withstand heat, chemicals, scratches and repeated use without breaking easily.

Companies use ABS to make car dashboards, refrigerator and air-conditioner parts, electronics and medical equipment because it is durable, easy to shape and provides a smooth finish.

The deets: the new line will produce 70,000 tonnes annually and is expected to be mechanically completed by December 2028.

Supreme Petrochem already operates one mass ABS line with the same capacity. Once the second line is completed, its total annual capacity will double from 70,000 tonnes to 1.4 lakh tonnes.

Share

4. Why PVR is betting on cheaper Multiplexes? 🎭🎬

PVR INOX is bringing cheaper multiplexes to smaller Indian towns, with ticket prices targeted at ₹150–175.

Its new SMART Cinema format costs around ₹1.9 crore per screen to build, compared with ₹2.5–3 crore for a conventional multiplex. The company has identified roughly 300 potential cities for expansion.

But India has an interesting problem. Despite having just 7 cinema screens per million people, existing theatres are shutting down because of poor economics.

Full Story Here

5. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🪵 Greenlam Industries surged 10% after 2% equity changed hands through a block deal.

🛣️ Ashoka Buildcon gained more than 6% after bagging a ₹1,465 crore NHAI contract.

💸 IIFL Finance rose more than 4% as Fairfax likely exits entire stake in ₹3,463-crore block deal.

🎬 PVRInox gained more than 2% as CRISIL revised stock’s outlook to positive from stable.

☀️ ACME Solar signed a 150 MW hybrid power PPA with NTPC, stock up nearly 2%.

🛢️ India eases oil & gas PSC extension norms, HOEC gain nearly 5%.

✈️ SpiceJet hit 5% upper circuit as board approved ₹5,500 crore fundraising.

What went down ⬇️

🥇 Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance fell up to 4% each as gold prices sank to 14-month low.

💊 Caplin Point slipped 7% after US FDA classified its Caplin Steriles facility as “Official Action Indicated”.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

💊 Cancer treatment: Biocon received European Commission approval for its breast cancer biosimilar Pertuzumab, marking its fifth oncology biosimilar approval in both Europe and the US.

🌱 Biogas investment: Reliance Industries plans to invest ₹15,000 crore in 100 compressed biogas plants by 2030, converting agricultural waste into clean energy to reduce fossil fuel imports.

☀️ Green investment: Amazon plans to invest an additional $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, expanding its wind and solar portfolio beyond the $4 billion already committed.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the weekday blues get to you.

items.title: Financials lead the market party 🎉
items.content:
🗓️ Morning, folks! ☀️

Indian markets extended their winning run on Tuesday, with the Nifty 50 reaching a nine-month high. The Sensex and Nifty gained as much as 0.5%.

Banking stocks continued to lead the rally, lifting the Nifty Bank, while the Nifty Midcap index added 154 points.

The gains were spread across the market. Eternal, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank hit fresh 52-week highs, while eight other Nifty companies moved within 5% of their yearly peaks.

💡 Spotlight: Nifty bounces back big time 📈

The Nifty 50 index has recovered all its losses since the US-Iran conflict began in February, crossing its pre-war level of 25,476 on Tuesday.

And the banking sector is leading the rally, with Nifty Bank hitting a record high.

This is also Nifty’s best monthly performance since November 2020, with the index gaining 10.5% so far in November.

Foreign investors are pouring money into Indian markets, while companies are also reporting strong earnings. Nifty 50 companies recorded a 27% rise in quarterly profits compared with last year, beating expectations.

Let’s hit it! 💪🏻

1 Big Thing: Tata Sons IPO buzz lifts group stocks! 📈

Tata Group stocks rallied up to 9% intraday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) once again pushed Tata Sons to follow rules requiring it to list on the stock exchange.

What’s going on: Tata Sons is the main company that holds stakes in major Tata businesses, including TCS, Tata Motors and Tata Steel. Despite controlling one of India’s biggest business groups, Tata Sons itself is not listed on the stock market.

In 2022, the RBI classified Tata Sons as a large Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), a category that comes with stricter rules, including a stock market listing requirement.

However, Tata Sons has been trying to remain a private company. In September, the RBI rejected its request to give up its NBFC registration. Now, in a letter dated November 16, the central bank has again asked the company to follow the applicable rules, including listing.

Why stocks jumped: if Tata Sons eventually launches an IPO, the market could get a clearer picture of how much these investments are worth. That’s why investors are showing renewed interest in companies holding Tata Sons shares.

But there’s a disagreement: Tata Trusts, which controls around 66% of Tata Sons, wants the company to remain privately held. Meanwhile, the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which owns around 18%, could benefit from a listing as it looks for ways to raise money and reduce debt.

What’s next: Tata Sons is scheduled to hold a board meeting on November 26, where the listing issue is expected to come up.

Share

2. Sigma brings Spanish firepower home 🇮🇳

Sigma Advanced Systems shares jumped up to 5% after the company formed an India-based defence joint venture with Spain’s EM&E Group.

The deets: the new venture will combine the company’s factories and understanding of Indian defence requirements with EM&E’s weapons technology and engineering expertise.

Operations have already started, although the companies have not disclosed their ownership percentages or financial investment in the venture. Both partners will jointly manage the business.

What will it manufacture: with EM&E technologies coming to India, the two will together make

  • Remote-controlled weapon systems that allow soldiers to operate weapons from a protected position

  • Guidance systems that help artillery shells, rockets and mortar rounds strike targets more accurately

  • Vehicles designed to carry and fire mortars

  • Electro-optical equipment, including cameras and sensors used for surveillance and targeting

  • Robotic systems for defence operations

The why: Sigma currently earns a large part of its business by manufacturing components and smaller subsystems for defence and aerospace companies.

The partnership could help it move higher up the value chain.

Instead of supplying only one part of a military product, Sigma wants to integrate and eventually co-develop complete defence systems.

Share

3. Who’s driving India’s logistics boom? 🚛

Maharashtra has emerged as India’s top state for logistics, scoring 4.05 out of 5 in a 2025 assessment by India Data Map, followed by Gujarat (4.00) and Tamil Nadu (3.95). These states benefit from better roads, ports, railway connections and large manufacturing hubs, making it easier for businesses to transport goods.

However, this is not an official government ranking. In the government’s LEADS 2025 assessment, Tamil Nadu was classified as an Exemplar among coastal states, while Maharashtra and Gujarat were named High Performers.

Full story here

4. Stocks that kept us interested 🚀

What went up ⬆️

🛢️ Auto, paint and airline shares rallied, tracking the decline in crude oil prices.

🪙 Senco Gold ended more than 3% higher after the company reported record net sales of more than ₹2,426 crore during the Dhanteras–Diwali festive season.

💊 Laurus Labs gained more than 5% after management said promoters have no plan for further stake sale.

What went down ⬇️

🔌 Cable and wire stocks declined amid reports of price cuts.

🔄 UPL gave up gains after reports that the company may revise its proposed restructuring.

What else are we snackin’ 🍿

📈 Market access: BSE received US regulatory approval to offer BANKEX futures to US-based investors, allowing them to gain exposure to India’s banking sector.

💊 Healthcare tie-up: AstraZeneca Pharma India signed a letter of intent with Reliance’s Strand Life Sciences to explore healthcare collaboration opportunities in India.

💻 Tech layoffs: Australia’s Bunnings will cut 350 tech jobs as it shifts work to India and the Philippines through a TCS partnership to reduce costs and boost AI investment.

🏦 Bank strike: IDBI Bank employees have called a nationwide strike on December 3 against Fairfax’s ₹52,878 crore takeover deal, raising concerns over its valuation, funding and ownership.

🤖 Chip restrictions: The US is preparing new export controls on AI chips and data centres worldwide, requiring licences to prevent Chinese firms from accessing restricted AI computing power through other countries.

That’s a wrap! Don’t let the midweek blues get to you.

items.title: Anthropic pulls off the biggest IPO ever
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 6,136 new readers. Frontier AI is now public. Anthropic just listed on the Nasdaq in the largest-ever IPO, topping SpaceX’s record from just five months ago.

The debut minted thousands of millionaires overnight and came with a promise from CEO Dario Amodei that safety, not business or political pressure, will set the pace of its models and way forward.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Anthropic raises $81B in the largest IPO ever

  • Rowan’s Corner: 4 things that stuck with me from DealBook

  • Use AI to find a job and prepare to get hired

  • OpenAI’s agents now handle half its long research tasks

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

ANTHROPIC

The details:

  • At the IPO price, Amazon’s and Google’s early stakes hit $161B and $147B, and Sound Ventures, co-founded by Ashton Kutcher, turned a $435M bet into ~$7B.

🗽 4 things that stuck with me from DealBook

Rowan’s POV at DealBook

Rowan: I spent Wednesday at the NYT DealBook Summit, in a room that was a good mix of tech reporters, top AI execs, and Wall Street heavyweights.

Four things stuck with me:

  1. When Christine Lagarde was asked if we’re in an AI bubble, the room laughed nervously. I don’t think we are, at least not the dot-com kind. Back then, companies built capacity nobody was using yet… today, the labs can’t build compute fast enough to keep up with demand. Still, a room full of top execs laughing nervously is hard to ignore.

  2. Almost every speaker talked about Jensen leaving Nvidia. Musk compared it to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” It’s a reminder that even at trillion-dollar scale, the AI industry still runs on a handful of people.

  3. I’ve never heard Sam Altman push as hard for humans to stay in control. He called gradually handing decisions over to AI “a terrible idea” and said he doesn’t want to end up as AI’s Labrador, or his kids either. A clear shot at Elon Musk, who has said humans could end up “like a pet Labrador” to AI.

  4. Greg Brockman said the biggest differentiator between the labs will be who owns the compute. To me, that means the AI race is becoming less about who has the smartest researchers and more about who has the most chips and power.

  2. Ask ChatGPT to find five current openings. Check each role on the employer’s own careers page before adding it to your list

  3. Compare one verified job description with a redacted copy of your resume. Ask AI to show strong matches, partial matches, and missing requirements

  4. Tailor the resume and write a short cover letter using only facts you can support. Review every new claim before saving or applying

  5. Practice eight interview questions, one at a time, then add the application and next follow-up date to your tracker

The Rundown: OpenAI just released new data on how AI agents are speeding up its own research, finding they now complete nearly half of tasks on their own that would take a human researcher two to four hours, up from about a quarter in March.

The details:

  • Agent use is exploding, with the median OpenAI researcher running ~$2.4K of AI agent work a day, and saying they’d hypothetically give up 40% of their team headcount to keep access.

Why it matters: AI that builds better AI could make progress speed up dramatically. Humans still call the shots, but a sudden leap could come, like the breakthroughs AI recently made in math.

items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 12,783 new readers. Google spent most of 2026 being mocked for moving slowly. But something changed this fall, and it’s now shipping faster than ever. Maybe the key is, as Demis Hassabis put it, “alchemy at its finest.”

The company’s new Neon model is the latest step up both the periodic table and the leaderboard, carrying a mid-tier label but with scores nearing the industry’s best. With one researcher hinting at self-improving AI behind the pace, Google suddenly feels very, very back.

GOOGLE

🧪 Google’s shipping spree continues with Neon

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google just released Gemini 4 Neon, a faster sibling to its top-end Carbon that leads Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol on most of Google’s tests — marking the company’s fourth Gemini 4 model in under two months.

The details:

  • Despite its mid-tier status, Neon edges Google’s top-end Carbon on Artificial Analysis’ leaderboard at 61, trailing only Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra.

  • Google’s testing has Neon beating Opus 5.5 and 6.2 Sol on 16 of 19 benchmarks, with its widest leads in long-document work, office automation, and cyber tasks.

  • Neon is now live for Google’s Pro and Ultra tier users, and its API costs $3/$15 per million input/output tokens, a quarter below Opus 5.5 and full-price Carbon.

  • The night before launch, Google’s Minkai Xu posted “many people are surprised by how fast RSI moves,” hinting self-improving AI may be behind Google’s pace.

Why it matters: For most of 2026, Google had every advantage (chips, cash, users) yet was painfully slow to ship frontier options people wanted. Whether it’s recursive self-improvement (RSI) or something else, a switch has flipped internally, and Google’s run through the periodic table (Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen, Neon) is showing up in a big way.

TOGETHER WITH GOOGLE FOR STARTUPS

🚀 Startup School: Gemma and Open Models

The Rundown: Routing every routine prompt through frontier reasoning models destroys startup runways. Google for Startups’ upcoming 4-part live technical series gives you practical blueprints to combine open-weight Gemma models with Gemini across your entire stack.

What you will gain:

Secure your spot.

NATE’S NOTEBOOK

🚰 Nate’s Notebook: Ask your AI for more

The Rundown: Each week, Rundown AI educator Nate Grahek breaks down what he’s seeing while teaching real teams to use AI.

Nate: Our well pump died at the cabin. The nearest hardware store is 35 minutes away, so one wrong part costs me the afternoon.

I was on the store’s clunky website, sure this one would stump Claude. I opened the Chrome extension anyway and typed: “Here’s our broken setup. I need water coming out of this faucet, and you can only use parts in stock at this one store.”

Then I watched it work, page by page. It would pick a pipe, find out it wasn’t in stock, back up, and try another route. It was wandering the aisles for me until it landed on 20 parts from different departments that were all on the shelf.

I thought that was the whole win. Then I caught myself getting ready to drive over and find all 20 myself. Years of confusing websites have trained me to pick the hassle I know. So I let Claude fill the cart, too. It told me when it was time to enter my credit card, and the whole order was waiting when I got there.

If you won’t hand a coworker the tedious stuff because it feels rude, this one is for you. I’m that person too, and I brought the same hesitation to AI. I think that feeling holds people back more than their tech skills do.

Back at the cabin, I almost let it stop me again. My first ask for assembly instructions was fine. Then I pushed for something more ambitious: a step-by-step slide deck. Here are both versions with the prompts I used.

Try it this week. Install the Claude or ChatGPT browser extension and point it at the site you dread: your health insurance portal, or that old internal tool at work that’s never getting an API.

Ask for more.

AI TRAINING

💼 Use AI to rewrite your LinkedIn profile

The Rundown: ChatGPT can rewrite your LinkedIn profile for the job you’re moving into, but left to itself, it rounds your story up. In this guide, you’ll have it ask about your real results, write a headline, About section, experience, and skills, then check every claim.

Step-by-step:

  1. Copy your LinkedIn headline, About section, one role, and your skills into a note as text, along with two or three job posts you’d apply for

  2. In ChatGPT, click the Temporary chat at the top right, pick Unpersonalized, and paste a prompt that asks for up to 5 questions first, all at once, and says “Don’t invent numbers, tools, titles, or results,” with your profile and the posts under it

  3. Answer every question, and say what you haven’t done yet. Then, ask for three headlines under 220 characters and an About section under 2,600 characters

  4. Next, ask for five experience bullets that start with a verb and up to 10 skills your experience shows

  5. Ask ChatGPT to check everything it wrote, in a table, and flag anything you didn’t say. Use the corrected versions, and copy them out before you leave the chat

Pro tip: Before you paste anything into LinkedIn, turn off Share profile updates (Me, then Settings & Privacy, then Visibility) so your network isn’t told about each change.

Image source: Pika

The Rundown: AI video startup Pika just previewed Enact, an experimental tool that works like a live film set, letting users drag actors around, give them spoken notes, and move the camera while the scene keeps playing.

The details:

  • Users can set the stage by grabbing a person or object and moving it mid-scene, with the AI adjusting how it stands and where its shadow falls in the new spot.

  • Each actor is a separate AI agent with its own personality that responds to both audio and text direction and can keep track of feedback from earlier takes.

  • Once rolling, the camera is controllable throughout the live action, letting users make visual choices just like a director would on set.

  • Pika said its team was “startled by how much more real and visceral it feels” to make video this way, though Enact isn’t available to consumers yet.

Why it matters: A large portion of the world still thinks of AI video as “slop,” but the ramp-up in quality combined with control, speed, and cost-effective models has opened a new outlet for creatives. With real-time video now seeing similar gains, creating an AI video could soon look a lot like what directors are already doing in the real world.

▸ A reader built a ChatGPT adviser to research contacts

Today’s workflow comes from an Anonymous Rundown Reader:

“I often reach out to people I know very little about, whether it's an important email, a text, a potential collaborator, a volunteer request, or prep for a meeting. Researching someone used to take more time than most of these interactions seemed to justify.

Now I use ChatGPT to look into a person's public background, find real common ground, and plan how I'll communicate. The goal isn't to show off what I know about them. It's to communicate more intelligently and naturally.

I start with a prompt that begins: ‘Act as my personal research, communication, and rapport-building adviser.’ The full prompt also tells the AI to verify identity and important findings, separate facts from interpretation, and avoid inventing a background or assuming someone with a similar name is the right person.

What I get is a better-informed message, fewer misunderstandings, and a clear record I can return to when the relationship continues.”

🚀 OpenAI drops GPT-6.2 Astra, Sol to mixed fanfare

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, upgrades to its top and everyday models aimed at professional work, and the launch drew sharp criticism from early testers who found them lacking against Anthropic’s current lineup.

The details:

  • Astra now sits ahead of Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon and behind only Fable 5.2 on independent tester Artificial Analysis’s ranking, a 5-point climb since September.

  • The cheaper Sol now scores on par with September’s GPT-6 Astra on that same ranking, while costing roughly 15% as much to finish each task.

  • Astra tops tests in science, legal work, robotics, and 3D builds, but shows no meaningful upgrade in coding, with Sol actually regressing from GPT-6.1.

  • OpenAI’s own assessment put Astra at its “High” threshold for AI self-improvement capabilities, a first for any model it has released publicly.

  • Several testers panned the models, with one calling it “the worst model OpenAI has ever released” and others criticizing its hard-to-read answers and coding.

Why it matters: The sentiment on this release was ugly, and probably not what OpenAI hoped for in front of its biggest rival’s IPO. Anything short of passing the latest Claude releases was likely going to be a letdown, and with Anthropic about to get a fresh war chest from Wall Street, OpenAI’s next answer can’t be another No. 2.

The Rundown: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang just made his first public statement since his resignation last week, apologizing for his “serious mistakes” and leaving the door open for a return to the company.

The details:

  • Huang wrote that he “created problems for the Board” and will cooperate with its probe, without mentioning China, Alice Huang, or the reported affairs.

  • Huang said he would “be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO” if it is “in the best interest of our shareholders, employees, the company, and America.”

  • In addition to a petition with over 188K signatures, Nvidia employee Nader Khalil warned the board that “irreplaceable talent… is now contemplating departing.”

  • Colette Kress spoke for the first time as acting CEO on Nvidia’s Tuesday earnings call, saying “our momentum is real” and “our passion to innovate will not change.”

Why it matters: Board chair Harvey Jones said the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” but the noise in the tech world is getting louder. With his message seemingly aimed at Washington, and both probes and testimonies on the docket, Huang’s comeback may run through Congress as much as the boardroom.

AI TRAINING

🧠 Turn a spreadsheet into a data story with AI

The Rundown: Claude Data builds a dashboard from a file you upload, with every number linked to the query behind it. In this guide, you’ll turn a shop’s sales file into an editable dashboard, roll back a change, and have Claude draft a shareable data story.

Step-by-step:

  1. In claude.ai, click Artifacts in the left sidebar, then the Data tile under Make something new. Choose Import a file and attach a CSV, Excel, or JSON file

  2. In the Reply box, say who the dashboard is for and what they want to know, not only what to chart

  3. Click the Sources icon at the top right and open a chart’s query. Its Result lists the exact values behind the chart, so you can check any figure against your file

  4. Click the pencil to retitle the dashboard, or ask Claude for other changes, like grouping revenue. You can also open History and restore the previous version

  5. Ask Claude for a Scrollyteller data story from the same file, and ask what the numbers can’t tell you. Check its figures in Sources before you click Share.

Pro tip: Chart labels round off, so our $44,998 quarter showed up as “$45K.” When you need the exact number, point at the bar or open Sources to see the figure Claude used.

items.content:

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,143 new readers. When its test agents broke out in July and hacked Hugging Face, OpenAI called it “an unprecedented cyber incident” and promised to tighten security. California just filed its own account of what happened and wants to talk about it in court.

The state’s new lawsuit claims the AI giant privately owned up to more than 80 agent escapes, despite only 27 ever going public — and wants a judge, not OpenAI, deciding what safe testing looks like.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • California takes OpenAI to court over agent escapes

  • Trump set to crown AI ‘national champions’

  • Make your AI usage go further with these tips

  • OpenAI tracks how scientists really use ChatGPT

⚖️ California takes OpenAI to court over agent escapes

Image source: Office of the Attorney General of California

The Rundown: California Attorney General Rob Bonta just sued OpenAI over the company’s July incident, in which its AI agents hacked Hugging Face, arguing it came after weeks of missed warning signs and was one of 80+ times its test agents escaped.

The details:

  • Bonta says OpenAI dodged his office’s questions during a probe opened in September, with the suit marking the first by a state over the breach.

  • After agents crashed a shared tool on July 4, OpenAI resumed testing within days and missed the weeklong breakout entirely, the suit says.

  • California says only 27 agent escapes are public, though OpenAI admitted to over 80 and has notified dozens of outside targets, including a federal agency.

  • The state wants a court order forcing OpenAI to test more safely, plus $2,500 for each violation and any money it made from the misconduct.

Why it matters: Between the quietly growing number of escapes, rogue agent ‘swarms,’ and AI-assisted hacks, the public likely only knows a fraction of what’s actually happening across the web. Though the Hugging Face incident feels like ancient history in AI time, the fallout from it is still far from over.

AI & GEOPOLITICS

🇺🇸 Trump set to crown AI ‘national champions’

Image source: Images 2.5 / The Rundown

The Rundown: The U.S. is reportedly set to label over two dozen U.S. AI firms, including Nvidia, OpenAI, and Anthropic, as “national champions,” with faster export approvals and financing to sell American AI abroad, coming in the wake of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.

The details:

  • The designated “champions” could see U.S. officials advocating for them with foreign governments, a fast lane on chip export licenses, and federal financing.

  • The goal is a one-stop shop where foreign buyers get U.S. chips, data centers, and AI models as a single bundle instead of turning to Chinese rivals like Huawei.

  • Commerce chief Howard Lutnick will reportedly announce the picks while facing accusations of ignoring warnings about a firm tied to chips reaching China.

  • Commenting on Huang, Pres. Trump said a return as Nvidia CEO is something he “would not mind,” though he still backs ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for the position.

Why it matters: The Jensen fallout had officials pushing the U.S. toward tighter chip controls. Instead, Nvidia is still on the champions list, and Trump says he’d be fine with Jensen back. The White House clearly believes winning the AI race means selling more U.S. chips — an important position heading into Trump’s upcoming meeting with Xi.

AI TRAINING

🧠 Make your AI usage go further with these tips

The Rundown: Claude Pro's $20 plan runs on a five-hour and a weekly limit, and long chats and high-effort use both use it up faster. In this guide, you'll set up a leaner chat and have Claude ask you multiple-choice questions before it builds anything.

Step-by-step:

  1. Click your account button at the bottom of Claude's sidebar, then Usage. Note when the Current session and weekly bars reset

  2. In a new chat, click the model button under the chat box and set Effort to Low. Under + and Connectors, switch off apps the chat won't use

  3. Prompt: “Don't start yet. I want to [task]. Ask me up to five smart multiple-choice questions about what I want. After that, sketch the plan and wait for my go-ahead”

  4. Send your go-ahead and every change in one message. If a reply is missed, edit your message instead of sending a correction

  5. When a chat runs long, ask for a handoff summary under 150 words and paste it into a new chat

Pro tip: Using another AI assistant? Skip the Claude settings and keep the habits. The sketch-first prompt, the one-message templates, and the handoff work in any chatbot.

🔬 OpenAI tracks how scientists really use ChatGPT

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI published a study of 1,800+ scientists who used ChatGPT’s free academic pilot, with surveyed researchers saying AI lets them work ~2x faster at the same quality, coming as the company opens the program to up to 200K researchers.

The details:

  • Writing research code stood out, with scientists saying AI allowed them to work nearly 3x faster, and about 2x faster at brainstorming research ideas.

  • Scientists also leaned on AI for research ideas, with 23% of ideation requests asking ChatGPT to suggest a research question itself.

  • Scientists under 30 spent almost twice as much of their AI use on code as those aged 40+, while older users leaned on it more for teaching and admin.

  • OpenAI also announced an expansion of the free program, with applications for 50K first-come ChatGPT Plus grants opening on Nov. 23.

Why it matters: The AI-in-science hype train is frequently showing off the autonomous labs, thousand-agent swarms, and full AI scientists. But OpenAI’s data says the real use today is far more ordinary, with scientists using AI to read papers, draft writing, and generate code for experiments.
